findings.summary: HARD (ogs/CLAUDE.md §4.3): computeVanDerWaalsMicroPotential raises three unit-bearing quantities (specific_surface, nS, rho_SR) to the third power and n_l to the third/fourth power (lines 228-243), and computeIntegrableMechanicalMicroPotential / computeStrainedFilmEnergyPair square eps_v (lines 605, 915, 977) — all power≥2 expressions on unit-bearing quantities. §4.2 dimensional-consistency comments are present, but none of these carries the §4.3-required physical-magnitude annotation ('evaluated at a named state, with the quantity a reader can sanity-check'), which is the exact class of check the specific_surface m²/g-vs-m²/kg incident (CLAUDE.md §1.3, also live in this same diff, see the beacon_1a01_dsm_micromacro_inflow.prj finding) shows a dimensional check alone cannot catch.

findings.evidence: index.md:33-46 shows only mu_lR^vdW = A*Sa^3/(6*pi)*nS^3*rhoSR^3/(nl^3*rhoLR) and states 'setting K to its default of 0.0 reduces exactly to the plain van der Waals form (PotentialExchange.h:124)'. But CreateRichardsMechanicsProcess.cpp:703-714 shows film_pressure_coupling defaults to true and is forced true even if a PRJ sets it false ('Overriding to film_pressure_coupling=true'); RichardsMechanicsFEM-impl.h:706-709 gates the film-pressure fold only on 'film_pressure_coupling && isfinite(confining_pressure_p_conf)', and lines 888-893 (computeIntegrableMechanicalMicroPotential -> out.mu_lR += mech.mu_lR_mech, additive) show a mechanical partner term is added to mu_lR whenever a finite confining pressure is present, independent of K. All five shipped decks are mechanically coupled RichardsMechanics runs with biot_coefficient set (e.g. beacon_1a01_dsm_micromacro_inflow.prj:257 biot_coefficient=1.0) and therefore build a finite confining_pressure_p_conf, so the actual mu_lR used in every shipped run includes this extra term the page's equation omits entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document the always-on film_pressure_coupling term (and the fact it cannot be disabled) in the benchmark page's formula/section, or state explicitly that the shown equation is the bare vdW core and that production mu_lR additionally carries the mechanical/eigenstress fold whenever mechanics is coupled.
findings.summary: Benchmark page's vdW-only formula and 'K=0 reduces exactly to plain van der Waals form' claim is false for all five shipped decks: an always-on mechanical/eigenstress term is folded into mu_lR that the page never mentions.

findings.evidence: index.md's 'Benchmark cases' and 'Switching it on' sections (lines 23-94) describe only enabled, pressure_tolerance, hamaker_constant, specific_surface, micro_solid_density_reference, micro_solid_volume_fraction_reference, initial_micro_water_content, local_nonlinear_solve_mode, fd_jacobian_for_exchange, micro_potential_convention, macro_porosity_floor, micro_water_content_floor, potential_augmentation_prefactor/exponent -- nowhere mentioning film_strain_coupling, film_energy_route or potential_augmentation_prefactor_live_dry_density. `grep -rl 'potential_augmentation_prefactor_live_dry_density\|film_strain_coupling\|film_energy_route' Tests/Data/RichardsMechanics/beacon_*.prj` matches none of the five shipped decks. PotentialExchangeParameters.h:261-293 defines FilmStrainCouplingMode{Off,Kinematic,Equilibrium} and FilmEnergyRoute{Operational,Exact} with two whole new source files (StrainedFilmPotential.cpp 937 lines, ExactFilmEnergyPair.cpp 432 lines) wired into RichardsMechanicsFEM-impl.h, none of it reachable from any deck registered in Tests.cmake.
findings.suggested_fix: For an upstream-MR-prep branch, either drop the strained-film/exact-energy-route machinery until a benchmark deck actually exercises it, or add a line to the benchmark page (and/or Tests.cmake comment) stating these are off-by-default, untested-by-deck extension points, consistent with the disclosure already made in the unit-test commit message.

findings.suggested_fix: Either chain dmu_lR_vdw_drho_lR through the density whose sensitivity it was actually computed against (split the bulk and confined contributions and apply each to its own dpL sensitivity), or set use_custom_dmu_lR_vdw_dpL on this path so the pre-summed dmu_lR_vdw_dpL absorbs both chains correctly. This is a formulation/Jacobian-consistency call; ask Vinay before changing.
findings.summary: In the analytic Jacobian's !film_pressure_coupling Maxwell-conjugate block, dmu_lR_vdw_drho_lR is built by summing d(mu_lR_bare)/d(rho_LR) (bulk density, from computeActiveMicroPotential called with rho_LR) and mc.dmu_lR_mech_drho_lR = d(mech)/d(rho_mc) (the confined micro-liquid density rho_lR_exchange_input/rho_mc) as if they were derivatives w.r.t. the same variable. The combined scalar is then chained through computePotentialExchangeUpdate's dmu_lR_exchange_input_dpL via drho_LR_dpL (bulk sensitivity) only, even though the correctly-computed confined-density sensitivity drho_lR_exchange_input_dpL is threaded all the way into the function and available. So whenever use_micro_liquid_density_for_micro_pressure is enabled (the file's own recommended default) and film_pressure_coupling is off, the p_L Jacobian term for the Maxwell-conjugate mechanical partner is scaled by the wrong density-pressure sensitivity (bulk beta_LR*rho_LR instead of beta_LR*rho_lR_exchange_input) -- an analytic-Jacobian-only inconsistency; the residual/converged solution is unaffected, and the magnitude is bounded by liquid compressibility beta_LR. Distinct from the suppressed d2mu_lR_dnl2/g_cut item: that one is a missing-scale-factor on one quantity's higher derivative order, this one is a chain-rule mismatch across two different physical density variables being summed into a single derivative slot.

findings.summary: When potential_augmentation_prefactor_vs_dry_density (the K(rho_d) table) is configured together with a <dry_density>, the parse-time fallback scalar potential_augmentation_prefactor is computed with the table's K-LINEAR getValue(), while every runtime evaluation site for the live K(rho_d) path (effectiveAugmentationPrefactor / effectiveAugmentationPrefactorPhiDerivative in PotentialExchangeParameters.h) uses the LOG-LINEAR getValueLogLinear() interpolant. For a dry_density that lies exactly on a table knot the two interpolants agree (node-preserving), so no currently shipped deck is affected, but for a dry_density strictly between knots the fallback would silently diverge from the live log-linear value the rest of the code path uses at the same rho_d.
